title: API lemma lem_Bf_off_K expands the Blaschke product Bf off the zero set
intent: Capture the abstraction boundary of the Blaschke product `Bf`: one lemma, `lem_Bf_off_K`, states the expansion `Bf z = f z * ∏ (Blaschke factors)` once, off the zero set, so that every client of `Bf` rewrites by this lemma instead of unfolding the definitions `Bf` and `Cf`.

parent.name: lem_Bf_off_K

children.name: lem_BfCf
children.note: The only child that unfolds the definitions Bf and Cf; after it, no client unfolds them. Off the zero set, Cf takes its else branch (simp [hz_not_in]) and the product of Blaschke factors is left standing. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: Bf z expressed as f z times the quotient of the numerator and denominator products, off the zero set.

children.name: lem_Bf_div
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The quotient of the two products equals the product of the quotients.

children.name: lem_Bf_prodpow
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The product of quotients equals the product of the quotient raised to the analytic order.

applicability.goal_shape: An equality `F z = G z` where `F` is a `noncomputable def` (here `Bf`, a composite of `Cf` and a finite product) and `G` is the intended closed form; the equality holds only off a distinguished subset (the zero set `zerosetKfR`), which appears as a hypothesis.
applicability.use_when: A definition's unfolding is wanted by many downstream clients, but you want them to cite one canonical expansion rather than unfold it each time; the expansion factors into a short chain of algebraic rewrites (division over a product, division over a power), each closable by a single Mathlib lemma.
applicability.avoid_when: The expansion needs a case analysis or a non-algebraic argument (then the leaves are not single rewrites and the interface lemma hides real work); the closed form is needed in only one place (unfold locally instead); or the boundary statement is not yet the stable form clients actually consume, so it would be rewritten again downstream.

The blueprint states the lemma and its dependency graph explicitly: the node lem:Bf_off_K ('B off K') is proved "By \cref{lem:BfCf} and \cref{lem:Bf_div,lem:Bf_prodpow}" and carries "\uses{lem:BfCf, lem:Bf_div, lem:Bf_prodpow}".

metrics.how_counted: All three children close by a single rewrite/exact to a Mathlib lemma (div_mul_eq_mul_div, Finset.prod_div_distrib, div_pow); no child needs a further project lemma, so the chain below the parent has depth 1.

consequences: Pins the closed form: after `lem_Bf_off_K`, a client that rewrites with it gets the `((R - ρ̄ z / R) / (z - ρ)) ^ m` factor form, so a later result that needs a different grouping must re-split. The lemma holds only off the zero set: the hypothesis `z ∉ zerosetKfR R1 f` is a side condition every client must supply. Unfolding is deferred, not removed — `lem_BfCf` still unfolds `Bf` and `Cf`, so the interface lemma hides the definitions from clients but not from the library. The `congr 1` step silently assumes the two sides agree up to the scalar `f z` and one factor; if the statement changes shape that step needs re-checking.
